note: A tune that climbs to the high Do, learned from the tab and then from the neck. The old tempo Stage selector and Key selector are now moves (any key, 60 to 84 bpm in steps of 12, the neck block kept 12 above), so the text names no selector, the tempo is {{=bpm}}, and {{?key}} and {{?bpm}} lines say what stays the same. Each block has one feel to reach.

exercise.title: A tune to the high Do
exercise.why: A tune is a pattern of steps from Do, so once your ear knows it at a slow tempo, a faster tempo or a new key changes the frets but not the tune.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}, then play along from the tab. The third bar opens with four quick notes, two per beat.
Practice until you can hum the quick notes before you play them.
{{?bpm}}At a faster tempo the quick notes come sooner: if they smear, go back to the slower one.

Press Play below to start the tune again, now shown on the neck, a little faster. Play it from the neck alone.
Practice until your eyes stay on your hand and not on the screen.
{{?key}}In another key the tune sits on other frets, and it keeps its shape: the same steps up to the high Do.
